subtitle: Panglao Island's dive-tourism hub, named on the spot by a 1973 film crew for an actress who was swimming nearby, now dense with dive shops and fighting the erosion and pollution that density brings.
spike_statement: In 1973, a film crew shooting Esteban asked locals what to call an unnamed beach; they said Alona Beach, after co-star Alona Alegre, and it stuck.

levers.photo_tone: White quartz sand packed with dive flags and resort umbrellas, the water a milky turquoise close to shore that turns visibly cloudier past the boat landings, low afternoon light picking out the rocky point at the beach's western end
